knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The power is isolated, secured and proven off before hands go near the pump. A visual check, a protective device or a request to a swimmer is not enough.
A pit with standing water may be a confined space. Entry needs the confined-space procedure, a standby person and any permit. Entering alone or pumping out from inside is not acceptable.
Licence requirements vary by state and territory, and this lesson does not grant any licence. Completing a lesson gives no authority to do electrical work.

practicalCriteria: Isolation: on a supplied pump scenario, the learner isolates at the isolator, secures it, proves it off, and records the time and the person. The assessor checks each step and the record.

Confined-space refusal: for a supplied pit with standing water, the learner refuses entry, records the reason and asks for the procedure, standby and any permit. The assessor checks that no entry was made.
Fault report: the learner reports a supplied junction-box fault from outside the enclosure, with location and condition, and does not open it. The assessor checks the report.
passRule: Knowledge checks: at least 2 of 3 correct (a reading result only, not verified practical competence). Practical sign-off is separate and is given by assessor review of the practical criteria.
evidenceRequired: Isolation record and confined-space refusal record, saved and dated
Assessor sign-off on the practical criteria
stopWorkCriteria: The learner is asked to enter a pit with standing water without the confined-space procedure and a standby person
The learner is asked to open an electrical enclosure or touch connections with the power on
The learner is asked to repair wiring or rewire equipment
